text.opengl: Build the view matrix with `glm::lookAt` instead of the translation: a camera at (0, 0, 3) looking at the origin, with (0, 1, 0) as up.
text.vulkan: In `updateUniformBuffer()`, build `ubo.view` with `glm::lookAt` instead of the translation: a camera at (0, 0, 3) looking at the origin, with (0, 1, 0) as up.
text.d3d12: In `OnUpdate`, build the view matrix with `XMMatrixLookAtRH` instead of `XMMatrixTranslation`: a camera at (0, 0, 3) looking at the origin, with (0, 1, 0) as up (`XMVectorSet(…, 0.0f)` for each).

hint.opengl: `glm::lookAt(position, target, up)` builds the camera's axes and the translation for you. It is the same matrix as before, so the picture doesn't change.
hint.vulkan: `glm::lookAt(position, target, up)` builds the camera's axes and the translation for you. It is the same matrix as before, so the picture doesn't change.
hint.d3d12: `XMMatrixLookAtRH(eye, focus, up)` – RH: right-handed like OpenGL, +z points out of the screen. It is the same matrix as before, so the picture doesn't change.

text.opengl: Let the camera circle the scene: `float radius = 10.0f;`, `camX = sin(glfwGetTime()) * radius`, `camZ = cos(glfwGetTime()) * radius`, and look from (camX, 0, camZ) at the origin.
text.vulkan: Let the camera circle the scene: `float radius = 10.0f;`, `camX = std::sin(glfwGetTime()) * radius`, `camZ = std::cos(glfwGetTime()) * radius`, and look from (camX, 0, camZ) at the origin.
text.d3d12: Let the camera circle the scene: measure the seconds since the first frame with `std::chrono` (`static auto startTime`), then `float radius = 10.0f;`, `camX = std::sin(time) * radius`, `camZ = std::cos(time) * radius`, and look from (camX, 0, camZ) at the origin.

hint.opengl: `float camX = static_cast<float>(sin(glfwGetTime()) * radius);` (and `cos` for `camZ`), then `glm::lookAt(glm::vec3(camX, 0.0f, camZ), glm::vec3(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f), glm::vec3(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f))`.
hint.vulkan: `float camX = static_cast<float>(std::sin(glfwGetTime()) * radius);` (and `std::cos` for `camZ`), then `glm::lookAt(glm::vec3(camX, 0.0f, camZ), glm::vec3(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f), glm::vec3(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f))`.
hint.d3d12: `float time = std::chrono::duration<float, std::chrono::seconds::period>(currentTime - startTime).count();` – (sin t, cos t) · 10 runs round a circle in the xz plane; at 0 s the camera is at (0, 0, 10).

text.opengl: Replace the circling camera with globals `cameraPos` (0, 0, 3), `cameraFront` (0, 0, -1) and `cameraUp` (0, 1, 0), and `view = glm::lookAt(cameraPos, cameraPos + cameraFront, cameraUp)`.
text.vulkan: Add globals `cameraPos` (0, 0, 3), `cameraFront` (0, 0, -1) and `cameraUp` (0, 1, 0) before the `PushConstants` struct, and replace the circle with `ubo.view = glm::lookAt(cameraPos, cameraPos + cameraFront, cameraUp)`.
text.d3d12: Add global `XMVECTOR`s `cameraPos` (0, 0, 3), `cameraFront` (0, 0, -1) and `cameraUp` (0, 1, 0) before `class D3D12App`, and replace the circle and its time lines with `XMMatrixLookAtRH(cameraPos, cameraPos + cameraFront, cameraUp)`.

hint.opengl: `cameraPos + cameraFront` is a point straight in front of the camera, so it keeps looking along `cameraFront` wherever it moves. Put the globals under the settings, before `main`.
hint.vulkan: `cameraPos + cameraFront` is a point straight in front of the camera, so it keeps looking along `cameraFront` wherever it moves.
hint.d3d12: `cameraPos + cameraFront` is a point straight in front of the camera (DirectXMath overloads `+` for `XMVECTOR`). Globals, so that `WindowProc` can change them later.

text.opengl: Move the camera with W/A/S/D in `processInput` at 2.5 units per second: globals `deltaTime` and `lastFrame`, the per-frame time logic at the top of the render loop, and `cameraSpeed = 2.5 * deltaTime`.
text.vulkan: Move the camera with W/A/S/D at 2.5 units per second: globals `deltaTime` and `lastFrame`, the per-frame time logic in `mainLoop()`, and a member `processInput()` (Escape closes) called after `glfwPollEvents()`.
text.d3d12: Move the camera with W/A/S/D: a global `bool keys[256]` set on `WM_KEYDOWN` and cleared on a new `WM_KEYUP` case; at the start of `OnUpdate` compute `deltaTime` with `std::chrono` and move `cameraPos` by `2.5f * deltaTime`.

hint.opengl: `float currentFrame = static_cast<float>(glfwGetTime()); deltaTime = currentFrame - lastFrame; lastFrame = currentFrame;` – W/S move along `cameraFront`, A/D along `glm::normalize(glm::cross(cameraFront, cameraUp))`.
hint.vulkan: `float cameraSpeed = 2.5f * deltaTime;` – W/S move along `cameraFront`, A/D along `glm::normalize(glm::cross(cameraFront, cameraUp))`, the camera's right vector.
hint.d3d12: `keys[static_cast<UINT8>(wParam)] = true;` – a letter's virtual-key code is its capital (`keys['W']`). A/D move along `XMVector3Normalize(XMVector3Cross(cameraFront, cameraUp))`.

text.opengl: Look around with the mouse: capture the cursor, register a `mouse_callback` that turns the mouse movement into `yaw`/`pitch` (sensitivity 0.1, pitch within ±89°) and sets `cameraFront` from them; use `firstMouse` against the first jump.
text.vulkan: Look around with the mouse: globals `firstMouse`, `yaw`, `pitch`, `lastX`, `lastY`, a free function `mouse_callback` (sensitivity 0.1, pitch within ±89°, `cameraFront` from yaw/pitch), registered and the cursor captured in `initWindow()`.
text.d3d12: Look around with the mouse: globals `firstMouse`, `yaw`, `pitch`, `lastX`, `lastY`, a function `OnMouseMove` (sensitivity 0.1, pitch within ±89°, `cameraFront` from yaw/pitch), a `WM_MOUSEMOVE` case that calls it and recentres the cursor, `ShowCursor(FALSE)` and `#include <windowsx.h>`.

hint.opengl: `glfwSetCursorPosCallback(window, mouse_callback);` and `glfwSetInputMode(window, GLFW_CURSOR, GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED);`. Yaw starts at -90°; the y offset is reversed (`lastY - ypos`) because window y grows downwards.
hint.vulkan: Register right after `glfwCreateWindow`: `glfwSetCursorPosCallback(window, mouse_callback);` and `glfwSetInputMode(window, GLFW_CURSOR, GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED);`. Yaw starts at -90°; the y offset is `lastY - ypos`.
hint.d3d12: Only while `GetForegroundWindow() == hWnd`. Read the position with `GET_X_LPARAM`/`GET_Y_LPARAM`; set `lastX`/`lastY` to the centre before `SetCursorPos`, so the jump back has an offset of 0.

text.opengl: Zoom with the scroll wheel: a global `float fov = 45.0f;` that a `scroll_callback` decreases by `yoffset`, kept between 1 and 45, and `glm::radians(fov)` in the projection.
text.vulkan: Zoom with the scroll wheel: a global `float fov = 45.0f;` that a free function `scroll_callback` decreases by `yoffset`, kept between 1 and 45, registered in `initWindow()`, and `glm::radians(fov)` in `ubo.proj`.
text.d3d12: Zoom with the mouse wheel: a global `float fov = 45.0f;`, a function `OnMouseWheel` that subtracts the notches and keeps fov between 1 and 45, a `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` case that calls it, and `XMConvertToRadians(fov)` in the projection.

hint.opengl: `glfwSetScrollCallback(window, scroll_callback);` – `fov -= (float)yoffset;` then clamp. The projection is already set every frame.
hint.vulkan: `glfwSetScrollCallback(window, scroll_callback);` – `fov -= static_cast<float>(yoffset);` then clamp. `updateUniformBuffer()` already rebuilds the projection every frame.
hint.d3d12: `OnMouseWheel(static_cast<float>(GET_WHEEL_DELTA_WPARAM(wParam)) / WHEEL_DELTA);` – one notch is `WHEEL_DELTA` (120); away from you is positive and zooms in.
